questions.q: What is the general syntax shape of a GRANT statement in Unity Catalog?
options: ALLOW privilege_types FOR principal ON securable_object
GRANT privilege_types ON securable_object TO principal
GRANT principal ON securable_object TO privilege_types
GRANT securable_object TO principal ON privilege_types
questions.explain: Unity Catalog's real GRANT syntax is GRANT privilege_types ON securable_object TO principal.

questions.q: Why isn't SELECT alone enough to let a principal read a table?
options: USE CATALOG on the catalog and USE SCHEMA on the schema are also required as usage privileges before SELECT takes effect
Tables require a MANAGE privilege instead of SELECT
SELECT is deprecated and REVOKE must be run first
SELECT only works for views, never for tables
questions.explain: Reading a table requires the full chain: USE CATALOG on the catalog, USE SCHEMA on the schema, and SELECT on the table itself — all three.

questions.q: Which privileges does ALL PRIVILEGES deliberately exclude?
options: ALL PRIVILEGES excludes nothing; it grants every privilege that will ever exist
SELECT and MODIFY
USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA
MANAGE, READ METADATA, EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA, and EXTERNAL USE LOCATION
questions.explain: To avoid accidental privilege escalation, ALL PRIVILEGES does not include MANAGE, READ METADATA, EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA, or EXTERNAL USE LOCATION — those must be granted explicitly.

questions.q: What is the correct syntax to undo a previously granted SELECT privilege?
options: GRANT NOT SELECT ON TABLE t TO principal;
DELETE SELECT ON TABLE t FOR principal;
REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE t FROM principal;
UNGRANT SELECT ON TABLE t TO principal;
questions.explain: REVOKE mirrors GRANT's syntax exactly, using FROM instead of TO: REVOKE privilege_types ON securable_object FROM principal.

questions.q: In Catalog Explorer's Request permissions dialog, what do the privilege checkboxes (USE CATALOG, SELECT, MODIFY, etc.) represent?
options: Deprecated privilege names kept for backward compatibility
The exact same real privilege names used in a SQL GRANT statement
UI-only labels with no SQL equivalent
Role names, not individual privileges
questions.explain: The UI and SQL are two views of the same privilege model — every checkbox name is the literal privilege keyword you'd use after GRANT.
